title: RAW INCOMPLETE: count a nominal collection by complete primitive-stem copies, with one outer property suffix
summary: An invented teaching convention writes a countable noun's complete primitive lexical stem n times inside one nominal word to denote exactly n distinct members. An explicitly separated outer property suffix applies to every member and is written once. A written ALL mode lifts a learned individual predicate over the Cartesian product of its argument collections; NOT has whole-assertion scope. This differs from947's iterated action heads, from952's named-set agreement endings, and from1201's uninterpreted transparent chunks. It is a complete restricted nominal/assertion lesson, but its22-working-sign physical carrier and historical-source coverage remain unpaid. No native root, ending, number or meaning is assigned.

design.purpose: Short inventory or spatial/property assertions that preserve an explicitly supplied small exact count while repeating only the familiar noun stem. The learner does not need a separate plural or numeral form for every noun. Large counts are deliberately expensive; this is not a general compression claim.
design.domain: Present-tense factual assertions over nonempty finite sets of individuals. Each ordinary noun specifies a learned countable kind and an explicit positive integer n. Each argument may instead be an exact literal name denoting one particular individual. At most one learned unary property restricts each argument. Learned individual predicates have arity1,2 or3. Each clause explicitly selects ALL; optional NOT negates the entire existential assertion. No directives, tense contrast, conditionals, unknown cardinalities, zero, mass quantities, collective action or cross-clause anonymous references are covered.
design.ordinary_vocabulary: Open learned vocabulary is allowed. Every lexical entry pays its spelling-to-meaning pairing and its class N, J or V1/V2/V3. An N entry also pays its actual individuation criterion: what counts as one leaf or one vessel. A J entry denotes an individual property. A V entry denotes one ordered individual relation and pays all participant roles. A spelling never supplies its meaning, arity or countability by itself.
design.semantic_inverse_ceiling: The reader recovers exactly the declared assertion, lexical identities, counts, argument order, one-property restrictions, names, ALL and NOT scope. The reader does not recover an original historical wording or decide whether the assertion is true. This is not an automatic semantic translation from a corpus.

lexical_root_contract.teaching_spelling: Unquoted learned roots are nonempty lowercase a-z strings. Each N root must be primitive: it cannot itself be an exact power T^k for a shorter nonempty string T and k>=2. Different N entries must have different roots. V and J roots are identified by their fixed grammar positions and need not satisfy the power restriction. No natural source word is automatically adopted as an N root.
lexical_root_contract.real_cost: The primitive restriction is a real limitation on lexical spelling. For example mama is unavailable as an ordinary N root even if ma has not been taught. To introduce that concept one must teach another primitive lexical form, paying that new pairing, or retain an opaque quoted proper name where that is actually the intended content. The restriction is not evidence that a natural language had such a lexicon.
lexical_root_contract.power: For N root X and explicit count n>=1, write X^n with no internal space or marker. One copy is the ordinary singleton nominal; multiple copies denote exactly that many pairwise distinct members of the N kind. The number is supplied by the message, never inferred from a drawing or from a native repetition.
lexical_root_contract.unique_root: A positive power has one primitive root. The reader takes the shortest nonempty repeated block that covers the whole body exactly, checks that this block is a taught N root, and counts its copies. If no taught primitive N root supplies that exact power, the ordinary nominal is invalid. An independently learned whole XX with unrelated meaning is expressly forbidden in this same unquoted N channel.
lexical_root_contract.outer_property: After the complete power, optionally write tilde plus one taught J root, for example lumlum~dri. Tilde is a written teaching delimiter, excluded from roots and literal-name content. It is not a free native glyph. The suffix restricts every member of the complete collection and is written once. X~s and XX~s therefore preserve the same property while changing the exact count. The entire suffix here includes its delimiter; no native substring boundary is asserted.
lexical_root_contract.no_auto_merging: External spaces remain meaningful. X X is two independently supplied nominal arguments if the surrounding clause licenses them; XX is one argument with two distinct members. Repeated adjacent words, repeated clauses and repeated predicate occurrences are not fused automatically. A learned whole-power reading shortcut may be taught only with the unchanged count-and-kind expansion.

literal_names_and_unknowns.name_syntax: A nonempty proper name is enclosed in double quotes. A literal double quote inside it is doubled. Spaces inside the quotes are literal name characters. A quoted name is one nominal denoting its named individual, not a counted common-noun root. It may take the same optional ~J suffix after its closing quote. It is never counted by repeated spelling.
literal_names_and_unknowns.name_inventory: The inherited83-character literal domain is a-z, A-Z, äöüßÄÖÜẞ, digits0-9, period, comma, semicolon, colon, exclamation, question mark, parentheses, hyphen, slash, apostrophe, double quote and space. An unsupported character is an explicit input stop. Quote doubling is actual written cost in this Roman lesson; a future22-sign carrier must encode every admitted character and every control.
literal_names_and_unknowns.unknown_names: The name Tava Ada is retained exactly as Tava Ada; no kind, activity, number greater than one or lexical meaning is inferred from the spelling. Repeated identical literal names designate the same named individual; unequal names are not automatically known to designate different individuals.
literal_names_and_unknowns.unknown_common_terms: A genuinely unfamiliar common kind, property or predicate requires a separately learned definition, category and where applicable count unit or valency before it can be used as such. Merely quoting its spelling as a proper name does not preserve an unknown predicate or common-noun meaning. Such unsupported source input must remain outside this lesson until its lexical knowledge is paid; no hidden whole-clause quotation or universal29-root paraphrase is supplied.

exact_teaching_grammar.NP: (taught N root)^n or one quoted name, followed optionally by ~ plus one taught J root; n>=1. No nested nominal power, multiple property suffixes, implicit class conversion or empty NP.
exact_teaching_grammar.clause: [NOT followed by one space] ALL followed by one space, one taught V root, then exactly its arity's number of complete NPs in declared participant order, separated by spaces, then a written period. NOT and ALL are uppercase reserved controls, not lowercase lexical roots. A period inside a quoted name is literal and cannot close the clause.
exact_teaching_grammar.text: An ordered sequence of complete clauses. No punctuation or grammatical boundary is inferred from a physical line or paragraph. Anonymous collections are newly quantified in each NP occurrence; previous text supplies no hidden members, topic or reset.
exact_teaching_grammar.line_handling: In the Roman teaching display, physical wrapping is permitted only at external spaces or after a completed clause; a name or long nominal remains unbroken. If a word cannot fit on the available writing surface, stop this teaching inscription. There is no invisible continuation bit. A full22-working-sign script still needs a paid overwide-word convention and is not supplied here.

set_to_predicate_interface.NP_value: An ordinary nominal introduces a witness set S with cardinality n, all members satisfying N and, if present, J. A name supplies the singleton of its literal referent, subject to any written J restriction. Distinct members are required within a counted set; different argument sets may overlap unless the learned relation or explicit content forbids it. No unnamed member list or order is claimed.
set_to_predicate_interface.ALL: For a predicate P with a argument positions, the positive assertion is: there exist collections S1..Sa satisfying their written NP descriptions, and P(x1,...,xa) holds for every tuple in S1×...×Sa. This Cartesian distributive reading is fixed and explicitly signalled by ALL. It is never an unspoken collective event, a pairing/matching relation, or a distribution chosen by the reader.
set_to_predicate_interface.NOT: NOT negates that entire existential ALL assertion, including its quantified witness collections and NP restrictions. It does not assert that the nouns exist but are wet, that the opposite relation holds, or that an action is prohibited. No inner property negation or separate verbal negation is available in this lesson.
set_to_predicate_interface.identity: Repeated ordinary NPs do not promise the same members. If an input needs the exact same anonymous collection in a later clause, this grammar cannot silently retain it; a separately written reference/binding mechanism would be a changed contract. Repeated proper names preserve only their declared individual identity, not an entire preceding message.
set_to_predicate_interface.mass_and_collective_limits: Water is not silently split into two portions. A separately learned unit such as cup-of-water could be countable but pays its own content and lexical definition. Two persons jointly lift one vessel is not equivalent to ALL lift two-persons one-vessel; the latter says each person individually lifts it. The collective input is outside this lesson rather than compressed under the wrong semantics.

write: Check that the interpreted input is inside the stated assertion domain and every ordinary lexeme is learned with the required class and individual semantics.
Write NOT only if the input negates the entire assertion; write ALL, the complete predicate root and one space.

For each participant, write the primitive noun root exactly its explicitly supplied count times, or spell its whole singleton proper name in quotes. Append the single property suffix once if present. Keep the participant spaces and order.
Write the final period. Start any further clause explicitly; do not remember an unspoken topic, count or member set.
read: Read the optional NOT, required ALL and learned predicate; its entry determines exactly how many ordered NPs follow.

At each ordinary NP, separate any ~property suffix, identify the primitive root of the entire remaining body, look it up as an N and count full copies. At a quotation, preserve the complete escaped name as one individual.
Build each exact-cardinality collection description, applying the suffix to every member. Apply the one fixed ALL semantics to the predicate's ordered positions.
Close at the written period and apply any outer NOT. No native word, hidden sentence boundary or privately known source analysis is consulted.

invented_lexicon_for_demonstration.lum: N: one countable leaf; no botanical species is implicit
invented_lexicon_for_demonstration.tek: N: one vessel; count unit is a vessel, not its volume
invented_lexicon_for_demonstration.dri: J: dry as a learned unary physical property
invented_lexicon_for_demonstration.nara: V2: first individual is beside the second individual; no temporal change or containment
invented_lexicon_for_demonstration.cold: V1: individual is cold as a learned unary property

complete_hand_examples.readback: There are exactly two distinct dry leaves in the chosen first-argument witness set, and each lies beside the individual literally named Tava Ada. This existential claim does not assert that only two dry leaves exist in the world or that no other leaves are beside that individual.
complete_hand_examples.work: The writer recalls lum, writes it twice, then appends ~dri once. The unknown name's full spelling and its internal space are retained. The reader sees one two-member NP, not two invocations of nara.

complete_hand_examples.readback: One dry leaf beside one vessel versus two distinct dry leaves each beside one vessel. The property suffix and the predicate remain unchanged. This is the explicit X+s versus XX+s contrast in the lesson, with s including the paid delimiter.

A two-member leaf set and a singleton leaf set satisfy beside for every ordered cross-set pair. No disjointness is added by grammar beyond the two distinct members within the first set. This contains adjacent complete NP groups BB B without an iteration head or a pending nominal-argument type collision. It is not a reading of any native BB B sequence.

There exists a two-member leaf set whose members are each cold; versus denial that such a two-member cold-leaf set exists. The latter does not assert two warm leaves. For an input specifying two already identified leaves, the identity information would require a different, explicitly paid reference contract.

The individual literally named mama is beside a vessel. Quotation prevents interpreting that name as two ma objects. The same mama string is prohibited as an ordinary unquoted N root; it is not accepted as an unrelated exception to the primitive-root rule.

costs.learned: Every noun concept and count unit, predicate relation and valency, property, primitive lexical spelling, ALL lifting, NOT scope, quotation/escape, property delimiter and clause period. Five lexical entries are supplied for this lesson only; a historical text would require its real vocabulary. Pronounceability or repetition does not remove lexical learning cost.
costs.written: A nominal with root length b, count n and property of length j uses n*b letters plus1+j if the property is present. Names pay all letters, internal spaces, quotation and duplicated internal quotes. ALL, optional NOT, predicate, inter-NP spaces and final period are written. No saved text length or fitted frequency claim is made.
costs.memory: One learned root and the current positive count while copying; the reader recognizes the root and tallies copies. Semantic use involves the written argument descriptions, not an implicitly stored preceding recipe or paragraph. Large n and long roots give long words and real tally burden.
costs.unpaid_full_writer: The Roman roots, tilde, quotes, uppercase controls, spaces, period and every literal name character have no fixed22-working-sign realization here. Overwide words currently stop rather than silently split. Common q-o entries, final-y share, broad terminal variety, short groups, long interior diversity, corpus coverage and all frequency/length gates are untested obligations. This module is not a selected native writer.

smallest_decision_changing_checks_if_lat: A source-side hand reader must distinguish a counted collection from n executions and recover the unchanged outer property; the collective lifting counterexample must be rejected rather than read as ALL.

The exact learned N lexicon must satisfy primitive roots. An allowed unquoted XX with independent meaning conflicts with one-count XX versus two-count X. Longest-match preference cannot preserve both messages.

An alleged application must supply counts and individuation from its source meaning. Ordinary unspecified plural, a mass quantity or a hidden previously named set cannot be admitted as exact cardinality without new written information.

A future physical carrier must preserve the declared nominal power and outer suffix boundary without free controls, and pay words that exceed a line. Formal B/BB alone would not establish a number meaning; known ol/olol and daldy/daldaldy remain unassigned observations. No native test is selected by this RAW card.

primary_predecessors_and_limits.retained: Multiple parses may preserve one expanded content, but an independent unrelated whole-power value collides unless separately written. The present card adds an explicit nominal count/individuation meaning and source grammar, not a new confluence theorem.

The old B6 short square failure and947 strict nominal-argument type collision stay closed. Here repetition builds a complete counted NP, not one of eight repeated action heads with nominal arguments to come. This is not a marker repair to947 and does not claim its known native BB B has become translated.

This card uses exact n and full nominal copies, no remote agreement, no mandatory name on every NP and no new native count audit.

Literal costs and conditional whole-word frequency limits remain.954's successful independent hand reading is separate from its fixed-control native countercase. No954 selector or syllable rule is reused or repaired; this card makes no statistical or historical gain claim.
